page: OVHcloud l40s-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured with 15 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9124 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz, alongside 90.0 GB of system memory (6.0 GB per core). Hyperthreading is disabled, dedicating one physical core per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. System resources are complemented by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU built on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 48 GB of VRAM, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary.

Benchmark results highlight extraordinary throughput in AI operations due to the Ada Lovelace accelerator. The server delivers top-tier performance in large language model inference across model scales, achieving 13,644.94 tokens per second on prompt processing and 605.12 tokens per second on text generation for a 135M model, alongside 6,030.41 tokens per second on prompt processing and 136.71 tokens per second on text generation for a 7B model. Even on a 70B model, it processes 884.03 prompt tokens per second and generates 15.72 tokens per second. In standard host computing, the CPU exhibits strong single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,941.0 and a stress-ng score of 3,043.17, while multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and web serving stay within middle-tier ranges.

The qualitative cost profile favors compute environments centered around deep learning inference and media workloads rather than general-purpose hosting. While the 15-core CPU and 90 GB of RAM offer sufficient operational headroom for data pre-processing and model loading, the primary value driver is the high density of the 48 GB L40S GPU. Consequently, the instance is optimized for LLM inference serving, fine-tuning, computer vision, and graphics rendering, whereas general web serving or database tasks would underutilize the dedicated accelerator.
description: OVHcloud l40s-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by 15 dedicated AMD EPYC 9124 cores running at 2.75 GHz, 90.0 GB of system memory, and a dedicated NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of Ada Lovelace VRAM. It includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmarks show exceptional deep learning capability, landing in the top tier for LLM inference across small, medium, and large architectures, while CPU compute and memory throughput exhibit dependable mid-tier to strong single-core marks. With its balance of dedicated vector-capable x86 cores and high-capacity GPU memory, the instance is engineered specifically for AI inference pipelines, graphics processing, and compute-heavy machine learning workloads.
